newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Champalimaud reported offering for Banco Totta.
newsitem.headline: Champalimaud reported offering for Banco Totta.

text.p: Portuguese businessman Antonio Champalimaud, whose group controls Banco Totta & Acores and Banco Pinto & Sotto Mayor, is preparing to launch a public offer for the outstanding shares of Totta, newspapers reported on Friday.
The Diario de Noticias said that the move would lead to the merger of Totta into Sotto Mayor.
Both Diario de Noticias and financial daily Diario Economico carried the report of the intended merger on their front pages but without giving a source.
Asked to comment by Diario Economico, Champalimaud declined, saying that "he could not talk about the matter," the newspaper said.
Officials at the banks were not immediately available to comment.

The possibility of an eventual merger between the banks has long been mooted, but Champalimaud said recently that any such move would only be carried out with the express support of virtually all shareholders.

Banco Totta's shares have tumbled some 25 percent in the past week since it posted worse than expected results for 1996, offering a proposed dividend of 135 escudos per share, down from 190 the previous year.
